summary: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY (no code modified) of the chauffeur-app runtime-error overlay on /chauffeur/home. Reproduced the red 'Uncaught runtime errors: Script error.' overlay after login as jean.dupont@demo.sb and toggling Online. Captured the REAL underlying error via page.on('pageerror') (the CRA overlay shows 'Script error.' only because the throw originates cross-origin from maps.googleapis.com and window.onerror sanitises it). The hypothesis 'Google Maps API loaded multiple times' is INFIRMED — only ONE main script (id=google-map-script, libraries=places,visualization) is present in the DOM, all other maps.googleapis.com entries are sub-modules loaded by the API itself. The TRUE root cause is an invalid SVG path string used as the car-marker icon in AdminGoogleMap.jsx — Google Maps' internal SVG parser (util.js) throws 'Expected number at position 63, found M' from marker.js.

ui_bugs.issue: Invalid SVG path string passed to google.maps.Marker icon.path. Google Maps' util.js parser throws 'Expected number at position 63, found M' when parsing the arc-command run 'a1.5 1.5 0 11-3 0 1.5 1.5 0 013 0M9.5...'. Position 63 is the literal 'M' starting the next subpath; the parser expected a 14th number to continue the implicit second arc (Google's parser does not handle the 0/1 arc-flag shorthand the same way native SVG does, so '013' is being read as one number instead of flag+flag+number, breaking the parameter count). This throw fires on every render of the chauffeur-position marker and is captured by react-scripts dev overlay as the generic cross-origin 'Script error.' (file: bundle.js:67582:58 in handleError).

action_items: FIX (main agent): Replace the invalid SVG path on /app/frontend/src/components/admin/AdminGoogleMap.jsx line 107 (carIcon.path). Recommended: use a simpler/valid SVG path or use google.maps.SymbolPath.BACKWARD_CLOSED_ARROW / FORWARD_CLOSED_ARROW, OR use icon.url with a PNG/SVG file, OR migrate to google.maps.marker.AdvancedMarkerElement. A safe minimal car-icon path that GMaps' parser accepts (no implicit-arc shorthand with packed flags): 'M -8 -4 L 8 -4 L 10 0 L 10 4 L 8 4 L 8 6 L 5 6 L 5 4 L -5 4 L -5 6 L -8 6 L -8 4 L -10 4 L -10 0 Z' (then scale=1, anchor=Point(0,0)).
OPTIONAL: Address the deprecated google.maps.Marker warning by migrating to AdvancedMarkerElement (low priority).

OPTIONAL HARDENING: Although NOT the cause here, GooglePlacesInput.js still injects a raw maps.googleapis.com script with libraries=places that is DIFFERENT from the useJsApiLoader (places,visualization) used by AdminGoogleMap/GoogleRideMap. On any page that mounts BOTH, the 'multiple times' warning will appear. Consolidate to a single loader (e.g. wrap GooglePlacesInput with @react-google-maps/api useJsApiLoader or share a common loader hook).
critical_code_review_comments: AdminGoogleMap.jsx L107: hand-written SVG path with implicit-arc shorthand and packed flag-digits ('0 11-3', '0 013 0') is fragile across SVG parsers. Prefer constant SymbolPath enums or icon.url to a static asset.

Multiple Google Maps loaders coexist in the codebase (useJsApiLoader in AdminGoogleMap with libs=places,visualization; useJsApiLoader in GoogleRideMap with different libs; raw <script> injection in GooglePlacesInput with libs=places). This is a latent bug that will fire 'You have included the Google Maps JavaScript API multiple times' on pages mounting both. Recommend consolidating.

CRA dev overlay's generic 'Script error.' is misleading. Consider adding a top-level window.onerror handler that filters maps.googleapis.com origins, or capturing pageerror in a Sentry-like sink to surface real cross-origin stacks during dev.

rca of the issue: Root cause: invalid SVG path in AdminGoogleMap.jsx carIcon. The path fragment 'a1.5 1.5 0 11-3 0 1.5 1.5 0 013 0' is intended to encode two arc commands using SVG's implicit-repeat shorthand with packed arc flags (large-arc-flag, sweep-flag must be 0/1 single digits). Google Maps' internal SVG path parser (QCa in util.js) does NOT auto-split packed flag digits the way native browser SVG parsers do; it treats '013' as a single number, which throws off the parameter count of the implicit second arc and at position 63 it expects another number but encounters 'M' (the next subpath command). The thrown 'Error: Expected number at position 63, found M' propagates through marker.js → common.js to window. Because the throw originates from a cross-origin script (maps.googleapis.com) without proper crossorigin=anonymous + CORS on the API loader, window.onerror sees only the sanitised 'Script error.' message, which is what react-scripts' dev-server error overlay then displays (in an iframe id=webpack-dev-server-client-overlay). Mitigation: replace the icon path (preferred), or use google.maps.SymbolPath enums, or use icon.url. The dev overlay does NOT show in production builds; this is a dev-only visual nuisance — but it does indicate a real (silent) runtime error that may also prevent the marker from rendering correctly.
